name: Baseball
description: Baseball is a thematic 7-Card Stud poker variant where 3s and 9s are wild, and 4s earn players extra cards. It is primarily played as a high-action 'Dealer's Choice' game in North American home poker circles. For the full technical specification, mechanical rules, and engine data, please see the master entry for Baseball Poker.

overview.description: Baseball is a thematic 7-Card Stud poker variant where 3s and 9s are wild, and 4s earn players extra cards. It is primarily played as a high-action 'Dealer's Choice' game in North American home poker circles. history.origins: Originating in mid-20th century America, Baseball capitalized on the popularity of 7-Card Stud and the national obsession with the sport. It became a staple of 'social' poker where the goal was to create massive, wild hands that would be impossible in formal casino play.
timeline: 1950s: Rules for wild 3s and 9s appear in regional US Hoyle editions.
1970s: The 'Match the Pot' penalty is standardized in many home game variations.
Present: Remains a favorite 'chaos' game in mixed-game poker rotations.
history.cultural: A cultural icon of the 'Poker in the Den' era of American social life.
history.evolution: The game's rules (3 strikes, 9 innings, 4 balls) are a direct mapping of baseball terminology to card ranks.

setup.players: Two to six players. Because face-up fours grant extra cards, more than six players risks running out of deck; the game is therefore capped at six.

rules.objective: Win the pot with the best 5-card hand using 3s and 9s as wild cards.
rules.gameplay: 7-card stud: two down, four up, one down. 3s and 9s wild; 4s grant extra card; face-up 3 requires match pot or fold. Best five-card hand wins pot.
keyRules: A 4 dealt face up grants the player an extra card immediately.
A 3 dealt face up requires the player to match the current pot or fold.

strategy.basic: Focus on collecting wild cards (3s and 9s). A 'natural' hand like a Straight is often useless against the high-powered hands of this variant.
strategy.intermediate: Manage pot exposure when you have a face-up 3; decide when to match the pot or fold. Use position and visible wilds to size bets.
strategy.advanced: Read opponents' possible hands from their upcards and the number of live 3s and 9s; balance bluffing with value when wilds are scarce.
tips: Keep track of the number of wild cards already showing on the board.
Be prepared for large pots due to the 'match the pot' 3 rule.

variations.name: Face-up 3 match pot
variations.description: A player who is dealt a three face up must immediately either match the pot or fold, or pay a fixed amount to the pot.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: This variant only changes the betting penalty when a face-up three appears; the underlying stud dealing engine stays the same.

variations.name: Face-down 4s extra card
variations.description: Some play that concealed fours also grant an extra card when revealed; timing of reveal varies by house rules.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: This variant changes when extra cards for concealed fours are claimed, which is handled in rules text rather than separate engine overrides.

variations.name: Football
variations.description: Threes and sixes are wild; a two grants the player an extra card.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Football keeps the same stud structure as Baseball but swaps which ranks are wild and which grant extra cards.

variations.name: Woolworth
variations.description: Fives and tens are wild; some play that a two grants an extra card.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Woolworth changes the special ranks and payments while leaving the base seven-card stud dealing pattern unchanged.

scoring.description: Standard poker hand ranking. Pot goes to best five-card hand at showdown.
scoring.winCondition: Best five-card hand wins the pot.

synthesis.shortDescription: Thematic stud variant with 3s and 9s wild and 4s granting extra cards. Best five-card hand wins the pot.
